n: This song of praise appears again, with small differences, as Psalm 18. David looks back over a lifetime of rescues — from Saul and from every enemy — and gives God the credit.
David piles up images of safety: God is his rock, his fortress, his rescuer. A man who often hid in rocky strongholds knew that his true protection was the Lord.

f.g: A mountain stronghold, like the ones where David hid from Saul (1 Samuel 23:14).

n: More titles follow: shield, horn of salvation, high tower, refuge, and Savior. Zacharias later used “horn of salvation” for the coming Messiah.

f.g: A horn symbolized strength, like the horns of a powerful animal.

n: David’s life lesson in one line: call on the Lord, and you will be saved.

f.w: I will call on the LORD

n: He describes past dangers as crashing waves of death and torrents of wicked men.

f.g: Compassed = surrounded.
Hebrew belial — worthlessness, destruction.

n: The cords of the grave were wrapped around him, and death’s traps confronted him.

f.g: Hebrew Sheol — the place of the dead, the grave.
Prevented = came before me, confronted me (not “stopped”).

n: In his distress he cried out, and God heard him from His heavenly temple. The rest of the song describes the answer.

f.w: he did hear my voice out of his temple

n: God’s response is pictured as a mighty storm and earthquake — the language of a theophany, God appearing in power as He did at Sinai.

f.g: Angry — here, God’s righteous anger at those harming His servant.

n: Smoke and fire pour from Him — poetic images of His overwhelming power, like a volcano or lightning storm.
He tears open the heavens and descends, with dark storm clouds beneath His feet. God comes down to rescue His servant.

f.w: He bowed the heavens also, and came down

n: He rides on a cherub and soars on the wind — pictures of a God who moves swiftly to help.

f.g: Psalm 18:10 reads “he did fly,” a very similar Hebrew word.

n: He surrounds Himself with darkness and heavy rain clouds like a royal tent.

f.g: Tents or canopies.

n: Out of the brightness of His presence, burning coals blaze — likely a description of lightning.
The Lord thunders from heaven; the Most High speaks with a mighty voice.

f.g: Hebrew ‘Elyon — a title for God as supreme over all.

n: His lightning bolts are like arrows, scattering David’s enemies.

f.g: Discomfited = threw into confusion, routed.

n: At His rebuke the sea bed and the foundations of the earth are laid bare — recalling the parting of the Red Sea.

f.w: the channels of the sea appeared

f.g: Discovered = uncovered, laid bare.

n: The God of the storm reaches down and personally pulls David out of deep waters. The vast cosmic power is directed toward one person in need.

f.w: he drew me out of many waters

n: He saves David from powerful enemies who were too strong for him alone.

f.w: they were too strong for me

n: Enemies confronted him in his worst moment, but the Lord was his support.

f.g: Stay = support, something to lean on.

n: God brought him into a wide-open space — freedom after confinement — because He delighted in him.

f.g: Open, spacious ground — a picture of freedom and safety.

n: David says God rewarded his righteousness. These words likely come from earlier years, before his great sin — or speak of his overall faithfulness and loyalty to God, in contrast to Saul.

f.g: Innocence of wrongdoing.

n: He kept the Lord’s ways and did not turn from God to idols.

f.g: Turned away from God in rebellion.

n: God’s laws were always before him as his guide.

f.g: God’s decisions and laws.
Fixed laws and decrees.

n: He kept himself blameless before God and guarded against sin.

f.g: Hebrew tamim — whole, complete, wholehearted.

n: So, he repeats, God has rewarded him according to his righteousness.

f.g: Repaid, rewarded.

n: A key principle: God deals with people according to their character. The merciful find mercy, the blameless find integrity.

f.w: With the merciful thou wilt shew thyself merciful

n: With the pure, God shows Himself pure; with the crooked, He shows Himself shrewd — He outmaneuvers their schemes.

f.g: Froward = perverse, crooked.
Twisted, shrewd — God matches their crookedness with His cleverness.

n: God rescues the humble but brings down the proud.

f.w: the afflicted people thou wilt save

f.g: Proud, arrogant.

n: The Lord is David’s lamp, turning his darkness to light.

f.w: thou art my lamp, O LORD

n: With God’s strength he can charge an enemy band and leap over a city wall — nothing can stop him.

f.g: A raiding band of soldiers.

n: God’s way is perfect; His word is proven true; He shields all who trust Him.

f.w: the word of the LORD is tried
f.g: Tried = refined like metal, proven pure.
A small shield.

n: Who is God except the Lord? Who is a rock except our God? He alone is worthy of trust.

f.w: who is a rock, save our God?

n: God is his strong refuge and clears his path.

f.g: Psalm 18:32 reads “He girdeth me with strength, and maketh my way perfect.”

n: God makes his feet sure like a deer’s on steep mountain heights.

f.g: Hinds = female deer, known for sure-footedness on rocky slopes.

n: God trains him for battle so that he can bend even a bronze bow.

f.g: Literally a bow of bronze — a very stiff, powerful bow.

n: God’s saving shield protected him, and God’s gentle condescension made him great. The Lord stoops down to lift people up.

f.w: thy gentleness hath made me great
f.g: Or “your humility” — God’s willingness to stoop down to help.

n: God widened his path so his feet would not slip.

f.g: Gave him room to walk securely.

n: David pursued and destroyed his enemies completely.
They fell beneath his feet and could not rise again.
God equipped him with strength for battle and subdued his attackers.

f.g: Girded = wrapped or equipped, as with a belt.

n: God made his enemies turn their backs and flee.

f.w: given me the necks of mine enemies
f.g: Made them turn their backs (necks) to me in retreat.

n: His enemies cried for help, even to the Lord, but no one answered — they had not been faithful to Him.
He crushed them like dust and trampled them like street mud.

f.g: Mud.

n: God delivered him from conflicts among his own people and made him ruler over foreign nations too.

f.g: Rebellions and quarrels within Israel, such as Absalom’s and Sheba’s.
Here simply other nations, non-Israelites.

n: Foreigners come cringing to submit as soon as they hear of him.

f.g: Foreigners.

n: They lose heart and come trembling out of their strongholds.

f.g: Fortresses, hiding places.

n: A burst of praise: the Lord lives! David blesses God, his rock and Savior.
It is God who gives him vengeance and subdues nations — not David’s own strength.

f.w: It is God that avengeth me

n: God lifted him above his attackers and saved him from violent men.
So David will praise the Lord among the nations. Paul quotes this verse to show that the gospel was always meant for the Gentiles too.

f.w: I will give thanks unto thee, O LORD, among the heathen

n: The song ends with God’s faithful love to His anointed king, David, and his descendants forever — pointing back to the covenant of chapter 7 and forward to Christ, the “Anointed One” from David’s line.

f.g: Hebrew mashiach — Messiah, “anointed one.”
